# @k8ordo/state

> Declare state by where it lives: `definePageState` (typed URL search params
> plus hidden history-entry state — the two faces of one entry, updated
> atomically over the Navigation API), `defineLocalState` (localStorage,
> cross-tab), `defineSessionState` (sessionStorage — the same store over the
> per-tab area: survives a reload, gone with the tab), `defineCookieState` (a
> cookie the browser writes with the Cookie Store API and the server reads
> from the request, so preferences render without a flash of the default —
> never a secret, it cannot be `HttpOnly`), `defineMemoryState` (a typed
> shared box with no schema, resets on reload). One zod schema per boundary
> place (url, entry, local, session, cookie) derives the server read,
> canonical links, salvage of stale data, and a client subscription with
> exact per-key change detection. Links and GET forms write the URL before
> JavaScript loads under any router (the server renders what they wrote
> wherever it reads the search); imperative url updates ride a
> Navigation-API-intercepting router.
>
> Like every k8ordo package it assumes React 19 and Server Components, uses
> only what has reached Baseline newly available, and ships no polyfills or
> legacy fallbacks.

When installed via npm, these docs live under `node_modules/@k8ordo/state/docs/`.

## Guide

- [Design Guide](GUIDE.md): the places and when each fits, the shared
  definition module, versions and migrations of stored rows, reading on the
  server, cookie state the server renders (and how it relates to cookies the
  server writes), updating on the client,
  batching and update handles, subscription granularity, router
  requirements and turning a page, links on the URL the router built, the
  one way to write each URL (a table shared with `@k8ordo/router` and
  `@k8ordo/framework`), reading local state before hydration, and pairing
  with `@k8ordo/form` for GET forms (whose URL is not the canonical one).

## Entry point

- `@k8ordo/state` — `definePageState(key, { url?, entry?, hash? })` returns a pure
  definition usable from server and client (`hash` is one schema for one
  value, the URL's fragment, read as the field `hash`; a fragment it rejects
  is an anchor and is left alone): `parseUrl(searchParams)` reads
  the url slot typed with defaults applied and invalid values salvaged
  (wherever the router hands a page its search — in `@k8ordo/framework`'s
  server mode a page that exports `search = listState.url` receives the slot parsed as
  `search` and is loaded again when the search moves; any other framework
  page never sees the search, and the url slot is read in the browser);
  `urlReader(schema)` is that reading for a url schema alone, the codec
  built once (what the framework's generated table calls);
  `href(url, values?)` puts the state on the URL the router built —
  `@k8ordo/router`'s `href()` (`listState.href(href('/products'), { page: 2 })`),
  a Next.js `Route`, or `''` for the page itself (`?page=2`) — rewriting only
  this definition's url params in canonical form (defaults omitted) and
  keeping the URL's other params; with a hash slot it sets the fragment from
  `values.hash` (none at the default), without one it keeps the URL's own;
  it adds no base (the router's `href()` has) and keeps the URL literal in
  the type, so the pattern is checked by the router — a rest param too,
  `href('/files/:path+', { path })` — and a typed route by `<Link>`. There
  is no `search()` and no `Register` here. Only `href` and `update()` write
  the canonical URL; a GET form submits every named field (`q=`, `min=0`).
  A same-pathname navigation keeps the scroll and the focus (a fragment
  too), so a pager moves focus to the results heading (`tabIndex={-1}`)
  after `update(…).finished`.
  `defineLocalState(key, schema, versioning?)`,
  `defineSessionState(key, schema)`,
  `defineCookieState(key, schema, versioning?)` and
  `defineMemoryState(key, initial)` declare app-scope state;
  `versioning` is `{ version, migrate(old, fromVersion) }` (type
  `Versioning`): rows are then stored as `[version, values]`, a row with no
  version reads as version 0, an older row goes through `migrate` and then
  the schema's field-by-field salvage and is written back in the current
  version by the browser store (`parseCookies` migrates but never writes), a
  newer row is salvaged and left alone, and a throwing `migrate` reads as
  nothing stored, is reported (`reportError` in the browser, `console.error`
  with the key from `parseCookies`) and leaves the row alone — an `update()`
  writes nothing over it and rejects its handle with the error; where the browser blocks site
  data, local and session state render their defaults and keep updates in
  memory until the next load; a local or session definition also exposes
  `storageKey` (the key in its storage area, `k8ordo-state:<key>`) and
  `inlineRead()`, a JavaScript expression for an inline `<script>` that
  evaluates to the object stored in that area or `null` before hydration
  (also `null` for a row of another version, when versioned) —
  unvalidated, so read only what you need with a fallback. A
  cookie definition exposes `cookieName` (`k8ordo-state.<key>`),
  `parseCookies(cookies)` — reads the values out of anything whose
  `get(name)` returns a request's cookie percent-decoded (`request.cookies`
  in a page and `cookies()` in a guard, a route.ts or a Server Action under
  `@k8ordo/framework`'s server mode, `{ get: (name) => store.get(name)?.value }`
  over Next.js's `cookies()`), salvaged like any read — and `cookieValue(values?)`, the unencoded JSON a server
  hands its cookie API (`cookies().set`, which percent-encodes it) when it
  sets the same cookie (`Path=/`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Max-Age=34560000`, never
  `HttpOnly`). `useAppState(definition, keys?, { initialUrl? } |
  { initialCookie? })` (client) works on any kind and returns
  `[state, update]` — state is the flat merge of a page definition's slots;
  `initialUrl` / `initialCookie` seed the server and hydration renders with
  what the server read; `update(patch)` applies synchronously, batches the
  calls a handler makes with no `await` between them into one write
  (url+entry changes atomically via `navigation.navigate()`, entry-only
  changes via `updateCurrentEntry()`, local and session via one `setItem`,
  cookie via one
  `cookieStore.set()`; memory applies per call), and returns
  `{ committed, finished }` promise handles (for non-navigating kinds they
  settle once the write lands, and a write that fails — the browser refuses
  it (a full or blocked Web Storage area, a cookie over 4 KB) or the schema throws on
  it — rejects them with its error;
  `{ history: 'push' }` exists only on page state and takes effect only when
  a url value changes).
  `@k8ordo/state/testing` is the entry for tests, kept out of the main one:
  `resetStateRegistry()` clears stores between tests, and `mountPageUrl()`
  stands in for a router there.
